title: The Fermi Paradox
summary: Over lunch at Los Alamos in 1950, the physicist Enrico Fermi asked, "Where is everybody?" There are hundreds of billions of stars in our galaxy, many far older than the Sun, and many with planets; even slow travellers could have crossed the galaxy many times over. Michael Hart argued in 1975 that the absence of visitors means there are no other civilisations. Others suggest that life is rare, that civilisations destroy themselves or stay quiet, or that we are simply early.
citations: Eric M. Jones, "'Where is everybody?' An account of Fermi's question," Los Alamos report LA-10311-MS (1985)
Michael H. Hart, "An Explanation for the Absence of Extraterrestrials on Earth," Quarterly Journal of the Royal Astronomical Society 16 (1975): 128–135
